what: The heuristic reconstructs the customer set, visited facts, location facts, depot, vehicle-count fluent, vehicle limit when exposed, and the complete routing-cost matrix during construction. Direct and return costs are obtained from grounded visit and return-to-depot operators using metric_operator_cost_from_initial_values. It then precomputes customer-pair Clarke-Wright savings. For each state, it reads all propositions once, identifies unvisited customers and the current location, forms a separate-route baseline, and greedily joins active route components using high-savings, degree-constrained, cycle-free links. The desired number of components reflects the current route plus unused vehicles when max-vehicles is discoverable. Goal states return zero, and states with all customers visited return the direct cost back to the depot.
why: CVRP routing cost is strongly determined by geographic clustering and by the expensive depot legs introduced at route boundaries. A Clarke-Wright savings forest captures both effects more accurately than customer counting or a single-route MST while remaining inexpensive because all static pair savings are precomputed. The degree and union-find constraints make selected links resemble disjoint route paths, and treating the current customer as a one-ended path accounts for the route prefix already traveled. The representative instances have complete metric-like distance matrices, clustered customers, and tight multi-vehicle limits, making depot savings and route-component count particularly informative for guiding search.
